conviction_note: The findings net to roughly zero (+0.1 after the lessons file, -0.3 before) and the scaled number is a small negative because p_up sits below 50 on two things the findings do not carry: this name sold its last two $0.17 core beats (-2.52% and +0.47%) and the two peer prints that landed on 10-13 showed deposit costs rising into a Fed hike; abs_move is set above the 1.76% median because a NIM guide has to be defended and the Lincoln S-4 credit figures reach the market on the 10-15 call inside the window.
bar: Q3 2026 core EPS consensus $1.29 (MarketBeat, event marked Confirmed for 2026-10-14, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/EQBK/earnings/) and $1.27 from 3 analysts, range $1.23-$1.31 (Tickflow, https://tickflow.io/stock/EQBK/forecast); company H2-2026 guide from the Q2 release: NIM 4.25-4.35%, non-interest income $18-22m, non-interest expense $94-98m, average earning assets $6.85-6.95bn (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227500/000119312526303176/eqbk-ex99_1.htm). Two estimate sources within $0.02 and a company guide, so sizes are not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest 591,717 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (FINRA published 2026-10-09), up 18.14% from 500,858, 3.36% of float, 5.5 days to cover on 115k average volume (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/EQBK/short-interest/). Not crowded; the sweep's merger-arb explanation is doubtful because Lincoln Bancorp is unlisted. Options: chain unusable (288 total OI, ATM spread 186% of mid), skew null, so the market makes no directional statement on this print. Tape: EQBK -6.2% since the 09-02 deal announcement against KRE -7.8% over the same span, so the run-down is the sector, not the deal.

findings.finding: The two regional/community bank prints that landed before this window (both bmo 2026-10-13) split on margin: FB Financial's NIM fell 12bp QoQ to 3.83% on 'higher funding costs relative to earning asset yields' (cost of interest-bearing deposits 2.88% from 2.81%) and the stock fell 4.2% that day, while Unity Bancorp's NIM rose 11bp to 4.67% on loan repricing (stock flat); Wells Fargo the same morning reported rising deposit costs; EQBK guided H2 NIM 4.25-4.35% from 4.36% and the CFO leaned to the 4.35% end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2025 revenue/NII miss (NIM up 9bp but revenue -3.4% vs estimate) took the stock -6.63% in the window and -11% after hours (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1138265385); Q2 2026 NIM +3bp with a $0.17 core beat bought +0.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus $1.27-1.29 was set before any Q3 bank print existed (Benzinga's late-August snapshot carried $1.31); if the market had moved EQBK on FBK's funding-cost read the stock would have diverged from KRE on 10-13/10-14 and it did not (EQBK -0.75%, KRE -0.9% on 10-14). A proxy: FBK is a Tennessee bank with a different funding mix, and a sell-side preview median for 22 regionals is NIM +1bp (RBC via https://finimize.com/content/rbc-sees-us-regional-banks-holding-up-into-2026), which contradicts the narrow read and is why this is sized below it.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo Q3 2026 release, rising deposit costs with a modest decline in non-interest-bearing deposits (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/72971/000007297126000318/wfc3qer10-13x26ex991xrelea.htm); Unity Bancorp Q3 2026 release points the other way, NIM +11bp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/920427/000092042726000050/unty-ex99_1.htm). Proxy, not a company-level number.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0), mid-quarter; on the Q2 call the CFO said 'in an upward rate scenario, I think we're well positioned to execute similarly to the last iteration' while flagging liability costs as 'the potential to deteriorate a little bit margin over time', so the hike cuts both ways for the Q4 NIM guide and the 2027 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline coincides with a hike; the Q3 2025 print (-1.85%) carried a margin-expansion headline and a repositioning loss.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike itself is priced into every bank; what is not visible anywhere is whether EQBK's maturing Frontier deposits (CFO: repricing opportunity 'over the next two, three, four quarters') still reprice down after the hike, which is the line the 2027 guide turns on. If the market had resolved it the Q3 consensus would have moved from $1.31 in late August by more than the $0.02-0.04 it did.
findings.independence: CFO Chris Navratil on the Q2 2026 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-14-equity-bancshares-inc-stock-1). Macro-to-company transmission the company has described only qualitatively.

findings.finding: The S-4 filed 2026-10-05 discloses what the 09-03 deal release did not: Lincoln Bancorp lost $(13.19)m, $(1.80) a share, in H1 2026; NPAs/assets 3.08%; Stephens assumed $9.9m of after-tax credit losses to be absorbed through provision by end-2027; Lincoln management projects only $0.8m of net income for H2 2026; the consideration is reducible for 'identified credit costs' with a $75m adjusted-equity closing floor and a BaaS platform in wind-down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal announcement itself bought +2.9% on 2026-09-03 ($49.57 to $51.00, Yahoo daily bars); no prior print in the baseline carried a target's credit.
findings.why_not_priced: EQBK moved -2.2% from the S-4 filing to today against KRE -2.8%, so nothing deal-specific has been repriced since the numbers became public; the 10-15 call (10:00 ET, inside the window) is the first time management answers for Lincoln's loss and marks. Netted against its own caveat: the $123.8m price is 0.9x Lincoln's $137.6m equity, so the deal terms already discount the problems and the market may read the S-4 as confirming the mark rather than as news.
findings.independence: Deal release filed as Form 425, 2026-09-03: $123.8m consideration, 77.5% stock, +5.1% 2027 EPS accretion ex one-time costs (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227500/000119312526381059/d152469d425.htm). Same transaction, different document.

findings.finding: A new 1,000,000-share repurchase plan received Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City non-objection on 2026-08-05 (about 5% of shares), replacing an authorisation that had 116,293 shares left at 06-30; the company bought 211,369 shares at $45.02 in Q2 and the CEO called buybacks 'no-brainers' when in range, with the stock at $46.5-51 through Q3 against $33.45 TBV.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline is tied to buyback volume; the Q2 2026 print disclosed 211k shares bought and moved +0.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public, the execution is not: Q3 is the first quarter the larger plan was live and the stock spent it below the deal-announcement price. If the market expected a 5%-of-shares buyback the consensus share count behind $1.29 would have fallen; three estimates in a $1.23-1.31 range does not look like it.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 release (116,293 shares remaining, Q2 purchases) at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227500/000119312526303176/eqbk-ex99_1.htm and CEO Elliott on the Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-14-equity-bancshares-inc-stock-1). Partly priced.

findings.finding: Credit was drifting the wrong way into Q3: nonperforming assets rose to $66.3m, 0.86% of assets, from $58.4m (0.76%) in Q2, attributed mainly to Frontier portfolio additions, with H1 net charge-offs $3.0m against $0.74m a year earlier; the CEO called it 'a modest uptick, nothing systemic' and named one house-construction credit, and provision fell to $1.3m from $6.0m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 ($6.0m provision, $0.17 core beat) moved -2.52%; Q2 2026 (provision down to $1.3m, NPAs up) moved +0.47%, so the provision line has been read over the NPA line.
findings.why_not_priced: The July numbers are in the price; what is not is whether the Q2 provision of $1.3m against a rising NPA count repeats or normalises toward Q1's $6.0m. A $5m swing is about $0.19 of EPS against a $1.29 bar. The two peers that printed 10-13 both cut provisions and reported flat-to-lower NPAs, so the sector read argues for the benign case, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: FB Financial Q3 (provision $1.4m from $10.1m, NPA ratio flat) and Unity (non-accruals down to 0.81% of loans) point to the benign case, URLs in finding 1; the panabee summary restates the 10-Q and is not independent (https://www.panabee.com/news/equity-earnings-q2-2026-report).

findings.finding: Insider tape since the last print is mixed: CEO Brad Elliott exercised options at $33.50 and sold the shares at about $51 on 2026-07-28 to 07-30 (about 17k shares), while directors Rogerson (4,000 shares at $50.00-50.25) and Schlehuber (989 at $50.98) bought in the open market in mid/late August, both above today's $46.48.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; no prior print in the baseline turned on insider activity.
findings.why_not_priced: Both are filed and small; the only content is that directors paid $50-51 eight weeks ago and the CEO's sales were exercise-and-sell at $51. Nothing in the price distinguishes a name whose insiders bought from one whose did not.
findings.independence: Director purchases aggregated at https://earningswhispers.com/whales/EQBK/insiders (last open-market buy 2026-08-21) and Form 4s dated 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-26 in the EDGAR submissions index (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001227500.json).

findings.finding: Short interest rose 18% to 591,717 shares at the 09-30 settlement (3.36% of float, 5.5 days to cover on 115k daily volume), published 2026-10-09; Lincoln Bancorp is unlisted so this is not merger arbitrage, it is a directional short built during the sector sell-off.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline; short interest was 151,800 shares in July 2025 (MarketBeat), so the position is roughly four times larger than at the Q2 2025 print.
findings.why_not_priced: 5.5 days to cover is a modest squeeze mechanism on an in-line print; it would be visible as a put skew if the option market carried it, and the chain is unusable (288 contracts of open interest).
findings.independence: FINRA settlement data via https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/eqbk/short-interest/ (same underlying series, carried in the sweep row); not independent.

findings.finding: The regional-bank tape is de-risked into this print: KRE closed $74.24 on 09-02 and $68.44 on 10-14 (-7.8%, including -0.9% today after the first Q3 prints), and EQBK tracked it (-6.2%, 10.2% off its 52-week high), so the run-down carries no company-specific disappointment and an in-line print meets a lower bar than the consensus number alone implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline run_up_20d -5.55%; the analysis in this repo finds the pre-print run-up does not predict the sign, so this is sized small.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price; the finding is only that the drawdown is sectoral, which removes one negative reading (a deal-driven de-rating) that the sweep row raised.
findings.independence: EQBK daily closes over the same span (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/EQBK?range=3mo&interval=1d).

baseline_tension: Nothing found cuts against the baseline: the option chain makes no directional statement, the -5.55% 20-day run-down is the sector's, and the findings net to about zero while the reaction history (beats sold, misses punished -6.6%) and the peers' funding-cost direction tilt p_up a little below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 5: the FBK peer-NIM read is a narrow proxy that a broader series (RBC's 22-bank preview median NIM +1bp) contradicts, so it was cut from -0.6 to -0.4 and the series is named in the finding
Rule 3: the Lincoln S-4 credit finding carried its own caveat (deal priced at 0.9x Lincoln equity already discounts the problems); netted from -0.5 to -0.3
Rule 7: short interest looked up (3.36% of float, 5.5 DTC) and recorded; not crowded, so no negative was shrunk for it
Rule 1: p_up moved from 45 to 47 to reflect that the name's reaction to beats has been damped in both directions rather than only on the downside; abs_move left at 2.8
Rule 6: bar verified to two agreeing estimate sources plus the company guide, so no cap applied
Left standing: buyback (+0.4), credit drift (-0.3), insiders (+0.1), short interest (+0.2), sector tape (+0.2), Fed hike (+0.2)
